This card practices キ and くわだ.てる. The separate verb たくらむ is dictionary-attested, not an obsolete or invented pronunciation. Its usual kana spelling makes it a recognition example here rather than an additional kanji-reading question. It often suggests a dubious or secret scheme; that tendency is not a rule that every use must concern wrongdoing.
企てる is an ichidan verb: 企てます, 企てた. 企む is a different, godan verb: たくらみます, たくらんだ. They are not two interchangeable endings on one verb.
Compare 全: its lower part is 王-shaped, while 企 has 止 below. The source indexes 全 under 入, but 企 under 人; a similar top does not give every character the same indexing radical.
危, danger, and 休, rest, also have six strokes, but neither has the planning meaning of 企.

staticMarkdownSelectors.target: It is a transitive ichidan verb
matches: 企てる means to devise a plan or attempt to carry something out. It is a transitive ichidan verb: the planned or attempted activity takes を. Forms include 企てます (くわだてます), 企てない (くわだてない), 企てた (くわだてた) and 企てている (くわだてている).

matches: The second sentence suggests suspicion about an unspecified plan. The verb also covers undertaking or attempting an activity, not only thinking about it. 企てた alone does not establish that the attempt succeeded.

企 supplies くわだ, the planning or undertaking element of this native verb; てる is the written ending. Keep the whole reading くわだてる rather than using the on reading キ. Learn くわだてる as one ichidan verb meaning "plan; attempt."

計画する (けいかくする) is a more neutral way to say "plan," including ordinary travel arrangements. 企てる can give a plan a more deliberate or weighty tone and can suggest a plot; it is not restricted to bad intentions.
引き受ける (ひきうける) overlaps with "undertake" when accepting responsibility. Accepting an assigned task and devising an undertaking emphasize different things, though their English labels overlap.

企む (たくらむ), usually written たくらむ, is a separate godan verb often used for scheming. It is not the contracted form of 企てる. For an ordinary schedule, 予定 (よてい) or 計画 is usually a better starting point than a word that may sound like plotting.

The dictionary also records an archaic tiptoe sense of 企てる. That label belongs to that sense, not to the planning verb taught here. The planning use taught here does not describe physically standing on tiptoe.

会社 (かいしゃ), "company," overlaps strongly. 企業 is useful for discussing the business entity or sector without focusing on a particular workplace.
工場 (こうじょう), "factory," names a production facility. A business can operate several factories.

matches: 大企業 (だいきぎょう) means a large enterprise; 中小企業 (ちゅうしょうきぎょう) refers to small and medium-sized enterprises. 企業 does not inherently mean a giant corporation.

matches: Do not confuse it with 起業 (きぎょう), "starting a business." That same-sounding word names the startup act; 企業 in this card names the enterprise itself, not any undertaking such as a household chore.
